newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Properties hit by higher DBS rates.
newsitem.headline: Properties hit by higher DBS rates.

text.p: Singapore Property stocks were dragged lower on Tuesday by DBS Bank's move to raise fixed interest rates on one of its housing loan packages, dealers said.
"We have changed the fixed rates in just one of our promotional housing loan packages. The rest of the housing loan rates are unchanged," a DBS spokeswoman told Reuters.

The change for the promotional package, which came into effect on Monday, called for a fixed rate of 5.25 percent for the first year, 5.5 percent in the second year and 5.75 percent in the third year of the housing loan.
This was slightly higher than the old package of 5.0 percent for the first two years and 5.50 percent in the third year.

Dealers said the move hit property counters traded on the stock market with the SES property index sinking to a year low of 614.47 before recovering to 617.30, down 1.88 percent, or 11.83 points, at 0850 GMT.
Among top losers was City Developments which plunged to S$10.30 before recovering to S$10.90, down 50 cents.
"I suspect the bank expects borrowing cost to rise. The bank is probably also trying to lower its exposure to property," Ng Yaw Tong, investment analyst with GK GOh said.
DBS is a leading player in the home loans market.
